lem-multivariable-laurent-ring-noetheria:
## Statement

For every integer $r\ge1$, the commutative ring
$$
\Lambda_r=\mathbb Z[t_1^{\pm1},\ldots,t_r^{\pm1}]
$$
is Noetherian and a unique factorisation domain. Its units are exactly the elements $\pm t_1^{k_1}\cdots t_r^{k_r}$ with $k_i\in\mathbb Z$.
def-based-string-link-and-labeled-link-p:
## Definition

Let $D^2$ be the oriented closed disk and give $C=D^2\times[0,1]$ the product orientation. An $r$-component string link is an ordered family of pairwise disjoint smooth proper embeddings $\tau_i:[0,1]\to C$, for $1\le i\le r$, with fixed distinct endpoints $\tau_i(0)=(p_i,0)$ and $\tau_i(1)=(p_i,1)$ and fixed product collars at the endpoints. Orient each interval from bottom to top. The exterior $X_\tau$ is obtained by removing the relative interiors of chosen pairwise disjoint product tubes around the intervals. The bottom and top punctured disks $P_-$ and $P_+$ are the copies of $D^2$ with the interiors of the endpoint tube disks removed.

Choose a basepoint on the outer boundary of $P_-$, a path in the side boundary of $C$ to the corresponding top basepoint, and basing paths from these points to the component meridians. Each end inclusion, with the chosen connecting path for the top end, induces a based homomorphism $\iota_\pm:\pi_1(P_\pm)\to\pi_1(X_\tau)$. For each string component choose a parallel path on its tube boundary from the bottom endpoint to the top endpoint, and choose access paths that close it to a based loop using the fixed side connector. The resulting element of $\pi_1(X_\tau)$ is its based string-link longitude; the parallel and access paths are part of the peripheral datum. The positively oriented boundaries of the endpoint tube disks are the designated meridian loops. Stacking two string links means rescaling them into the lower and upper halves of $C$ and identifying their matching endpoint collars; closure joins each top endpoint to the matching bottom endpoint outside $C$ and retains the component labels.

For a nonempty labeled oriented link $L=K_1\cup\cdots\cup K_r$ in the oriented three-sphere, choose pairwise disjoint closed product tubes $N(K_i)$, put $E_L=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}\bigl(\bigcup_iN(K_i)\bigr)$, and write $T_i=\partial N(K_i)$. A positive meridian $\mu_i$ is the oriented boundary of a normal disk, with the disk orientation fixed by the rule that the oriented tangent of $K_i$ followed by the disk orientation gives the ambient orientation. A degree-one parallel is a simple closed curve on $T_i$ whose projection to $K_i$ has degree $+1$. A based longitude is the class of such a parallel transported to the common basepoint by a specified path. When the positive meridians form a basis of $H_1(E_L;\mathbb Z)$, the self-meridian coordinate of a longitude is its coefficient on $[\mu_i]$. A preferred zero-self-meridian longitude is a chosen degree-one parallel whose self-meridian coordinate is zero. The choice, when it exists, is part of the peripheral datum; this definition asserts neither existence nor uniqueness. Changing a common basing path conjugates the peripheral group elements simultaneously.
def-maximal-abelian-cover-alexander-modu:
## Definition

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $L=K_1\cup\cdots\cup K_r\subset S^3$ be a nonempty oriented smooth link with $r\ge1$ components, and let $X_L=S^3\setminus L$ be its open complement. For each component choose a smooth fibrewise norm on its normal plane bundle $\nu(K_i)$ and a tubular map $\Phi_i$ from an open neighborhood of the zero section, fixing the zero section, together with a radius $\epsilon_i>0 whose closed disk subbundle lies in that neighborhood. Require the resulting closed tubes $N(K_i)=\Phi_i(D_{\epsilon_i}\nu(K_i))$ to be pairwise disjoint, and put $N(L)=\bigcup_{i=1}^rN(K_i)$ and $E_L=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}_{S^3}N(L)$, the resulting compact smooth $3$-manifold with boundary. The tube choices are part of the input. Choose a basepoint $b\in E_L\subset X_L$. Orient each normal disk so that the positive tangent to $K_i$ followed by its positive normal basis agrees with the fixed orientation of $S^3$. A **positive meridian** $\mu_i$ of $K_i$ is the oriented boundary of the radius-$\epsilon_i$ normal disk in one fibre of $\nu(K_i)$; it lies on $\partial E_L$, meets $K_i$ once, and misses every other component. Alexander duality identifies $H_1(X_L;\mathbb Z)$ with $\mathbb Z^r$ and identifies the classes of $\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_r$ with its standard basis. Write $G=\pi_1(X_L,b)$ and let $\phi:G\to H_1(X_L;\mathbb Z)$ be the first Hurewicz homomorphism, equivalently abelianization. The subgroup $\ker\phi$ is normal. The connected covering $p:X_L^{\mathrm{ab}}\to X_L$ classified by $\ker\phi$ is the **maximal abelian cover**; it is regular and its deck group is identified with $G/\ker\phi\cong H_1(X_L;\mathbb Z)$. Put $\Lambda_r=\mathbb Z[H_1(X_L;\mathbb Z)]\cong\mathbb Z[t_1^{\pm1},\ldots,t_r^{\pm1}]$, where $t_i$ is the deck transformation corresponding to $[\mu_i]$. The isomorphism sends each variable to its group-ring basis element; monomials $t_1^{n_1}\cdots t_r^{n_r}$ correspond bijectively to the basis elements indexed by $n_1[\mu_1]+\cdots+n_r[\mu_r]$. Define the absolute multivariable Alexander module by

$$
A_L=H_1(X_L^{\mathrm{ab}};\mathbb Z),
$$

as a left $\Lambda_r$-module under the deck action. “Absolute” means this is ordinary homology of the covering space, not relative homology with respect to a fibre over the basepoint.
lem-link-wirtinger-crossing-ball-cover:
## Statement

Let $D$ be a finite regular oriented diagram of a nonempty labeled link, with
$n\geq1$ crossings and at least one underpassing point on each component. Fix a
smooth height realization $L_D=\{(\gamma(s),\eta(s))\}\subset\mathbb R^2\times[-1,0]$
such that $\eta(s)=-1$ exactly at the $n$ underpassing points and
$\eta(s)>-1$ elsewhere; at each crossing the overpassing point has height
strictly greater than $-1$. Put
$$A=(\mathbb R^2\times[-1,\infty))\cup\{\infty\},\quad B=(\mathbb R^2\times(-\infty,-1])\cup\{\infty\},\quad \Sigma=(\mathbb R^2\times\{-1\})\cup\{\infty\},$$
and write $X=S^3\setminus L_D$, $A_L=A\cap X$, $B_L=B\cap X$,
and $\Sigma_L=\Sigma\cap X$. Also put
$A_L^\circ=((\mathbb R^2\times(-1,\infty))\cup\{\infty\})\cap X$.
Then $\Sigma_L$ is a path-connected sphere
with $n$ punctures, $A_L\cup B_L=X$, and $A_L\cap B_L=\Sigma_L$. There are
path-connected open sets $U,V\subset X$ such that $X=U\cup V$, $U$ deformation
retracts onto $A_L$, $V$ deformation retracts onto $B_L$, and $U\cap V$
deformation retracts onto $\Sigma_L$. The set $B_L$ is contractible. The small
circles in $\Sigma_L$ around the $n$ punctures normally generate
$\pi_1(\Sigma_L)$, and they still normally generate after any one circle is
omitted. The inclusion $A_L^\circ\hookrightarrow A_L$ is a homotopy
equivalence. Radial retraction in each chosen product tube identifies
$\pi_1(X)$ with the fundamental group of the chosen link exterior.
lem-maximal-abelian-cover-link-exterior-:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the data in the definition of the maximal-abelian-cover Alexander module for a nonempty oriented smooth link $L$. Let $i:E_L\hookrightarrow X_L$ be the inclusion of the compact exterior into the open complement, and let $p:X_L^{\mathrm{ab}}\to X_L$ be the maximal abelian cover. Then $E_L$ is a strong deformation retract of $X_L$, the restricted covering $p^{-1}(E_L)\to E_L$ is the connected maximal abelian cover of $E_L$, and the lifted deformation retract is equivariant under the deck group. The inclusion identifies $H_1(E_L;\mathbb Z)$ with $H_1(X_L;\mathbb Z)$ and preserves the positive-meridian classes. In particular, inclusion induces a $\Lambda_r$-module isomorphism

$$
H_1(p^{-1}(E_L);\mathbb Z)\cong A_L.
$$
lem-string-link-exterior-homology-and-me:
## Statement

Use integral homology. Let $L=K_1\cup\cdots\cup K_r$ be a nonempty labeled oriented smooth link in $S^3$ with chosen pairwise disjoint product tubes and exterior $E_L$. Then $H_1(E_L;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^r$, with the positive meridians as its ordered basis. Each boundary torus $T_i$ has a product basis consisting of its positive meridian and a degree-one section. There is a unique degree-one class on $T_i$ whose image has zero $i$th meridian coordinate; this class is primitive and has a simple closed representative.

Let $\tau$ be an $r$-component string link with chosen disjoint product tubes in $D^2\times[0,1]$, exterior $X_\tau$, and bottom and top punctured disks $P_-$ and $P_+$. Then each $\pi_1(P_\pm)$ is free of rank $r$. Positive endpoint meridians with the compatible accesses transported from a point-punctured-disk spine form an ordered free basis. For arbitrary independently chosen access paths, the corresponding meridian is $c_i m_i c_i^{-1}$, where $m_i$ is the compatible-stem meridian and $c_i$ is the recorded access-path difference; these conjugates need not be a free basis. In particular $H_1(P_\pm;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^r$, and $H_2(P_\pm;\mathbb Z)=0$. The exterior satisfies $H_1(X_\tau;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^r$ and $H_2(X_\tau;\mathbb Z)=0$. Each end inclusion sends its ordered positive meridian basis to the ordered positive meridian basis of $H_1(X_\tau;\mathbb Z)$. Consequently both induced homomorphisms on $H_1$ are isomorphisms and both induced homomorphisms on $H_2$ are surjective.
def-topological-linking-number-by-meridi:
## Definition

Let $K$ and $J$ be disjoint oriented smooth embedded circles in the oriented
three-sphere. Choose a closed product tube $N(K)$ disjoint from $J$, let
$E_K=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)$, and let $\mu_K$ be the positive
meridian. Since $H_1(E_K;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z[\mu_K]$, define the topological
linking number relative to this tube by the unique integer $a$ satisfying
$$[J]=a[\mu_K]\quad\text{in }H_1(E_K;\mathbb Z).$$
The chosen tube is part of the data for this definition.
lem-link-wirtinger-local-meridian-conjug:
## Statement

At an oriented crossing let $o$ be the over-strand. Orient the projection plane
by the rule that $(v_1,v_2)$ is a positive basis exactly when the ordered triple
$(n,v_1,v_2)$ is positive in the ambient three-space, where $n$ is the viewing
normal. Let $n_o$ be the positive in-plane normal characterized by the condition
that $(v_o,n_o)$ is positive in this plane. Call the under-side from
which $n_o$ points the source $s$, and the side toward which it points the
target $t$. Use a common basepoint above the diagram and paths in the upper
collar to the positive meridians $m_o,m_s,m_t$. Then
$$m_t=m_o^{-1}m_sm_o.$$
Equivalently, the crossing relator is
$m_o^{-1}m_sm_om_t^{-1}=1$. Reversing the direction of the under-strand
does not change the side-based equation.
lem-maximal-abelian-cover-cellular-chain:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $L$ be a nonempty oriented smooth $r$-component link with $r\ge1$, compact exterior $E_L$, and maximal abelian cover $E_L^{\mathrm{ab}}\to E_L$ with deck group $H\cong\mathbb Z^r$ and group ring $\Lambda_r=\mathbb Z[H]$. For any finite CW structure on $E_L$, the inverse-image cells and one chosen lift of each open cell form a finite-rank free $\Lambda_r$ cellular chain complex. Its first homology is the absolute multivariable Alexander module $A_L=H_1(X_L^{\mathrm{ab}};\mathbb Z)$, with the deck action specified by the positive meridians.
lem-link-peripheral-longitude-word-from-:
## Statement

Let the diagram be either a based regular string-link
diagram in $D^2\times[0,1]$ or a finite regular oriented diagram of a nonempty
labeled closed link. In string-link mode, choose the product-tube parallel to
be the blackboard push-off determined by the projected tangent, carried
through the fixed endpoint collars. Choose one initial strand on each
component. For the literal diagram word below first use compatible common-upper-collar accesses to all positive strand meridians and the induced endpoint accesses for the parallel; a common change of the complement base path is allowed. Arbitrary independent access paths and other degree-one parallels remain allowed, with their exact correction formula specified below. Traverse component $K_j$ in its orientation
(from bottom to top for a string link and once around for a closed link). At
each undercrossing $c$ of $K_j$, let $o(c)$ be the over-strand, and set
$\epsilon_c=+1$ if the traversal goes from the source side to the target side
of the over-strand's positive in-plane normal, and $\epsilon_c=-1$ if it goes
from target to source. If the undercrossings in traversal order are
$c_1,\ldots,c_s$, define
$$W_j(D)=x_{o(c_1)}^{\epsilon_{c_1}}\cdots x_{o(c_s)}^{\epsilon_{c_s}}.$$
For a string link, this word represents its based longitude. For a closed
link, it represents the blackboard parallel in $\pi_1(E_L)$. The preferred
zero-self-meridian longitude in the closed-link case is represented by
$$\lambda_j(D)=x_j^{-\operatorname{wr}_j(D)}W_j(D),$$
where $x_j$ is the initial meridian on $K_j$ and $\operatorname{wr}_j(D)$ is
the sum of crossing signs at self-crossings of $K_j$.

For the arbitrary-choice branch, write $a_e$ for the compatible access to the chosen meridian circle of strand $e$ and $a_e'$ for the actual access, after recording any endpoint-on-the-circle connectors. Put $g_e=a_e'a_e^{-1}$ and $y_e=g_e x_e g_e^{-1}$. The compatible word expressed in these actual meridians is
$$\widehat W_j=\prod_{c\text{ in traversal order}}g_{o(c)}^{-1}y_{o(c)}^{\epsilon_c}g_{o(c)}=W_j.$$
Let $a_0,a_1$ be the compatible accesses to the initial and terminal points of the blackboard parallel, with the fixed side connector included in $a_1$ for a string link. For a closed component these are the same access. Record actual accesses $a_0',a_1'$ and put $h_0=a_0'a_0^{-1}$, $h_1=a_1'a_1^{-1}$. For a chosen parallel $\beta'$ with the same endpoint coordinates as the blackboard parallel $\beta$, let $k\in\mathbb Z$ be its relative meridian winding, so $\beta'\simeq\mu_0^k\beta$ on the tube. A closed degree-one parallel is included; then $h_0=h_1=h$. Its actual based class is exactly
$$h_0x_j^k\widehat W_jh_1^{-1}.$$
For a closed component its self-meridian coordinate is $k+\operatorname{wr}_j(D)$, and its preferred zero-self-meridian correction is
$$h\,x_j^{-\operatorname{wr}_j(D)}\widehat W_j\,h^{-1}.$$
Thus arbitrary changes are retained as explicit transport and winding factors; independent access choices are not silently assumed to give the literal uncorrected product in the $y_e$.
lem-multivariable-alexander-order-and-sp:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and let $L$ be a nonempty oriented $r$-component link with $r\ge1$ and maximal-abelian-cover module $A_L$ over $\Lambda_r=\mathbb Z[t_1^{\pm1},\ldots,t_r^{\pm1}]$. Then $A_L$ is finitely presented, every elementary/Fitting ideal $E_j(A_L)$ is independent of the chosen finite triangulation and of the chosen lifts of its cells, and the order $\operatorname{ord}(A_L)$—the greatest common divisor of the generators of $E_q(A_L)$, where $q=\dim_{\operatorname{Frac}(\Lambda_r)}(A_L\otimes_{\Lambda_r}\operatorname{Frac}(\Lambda_r))$—is defined up to a unit $\pm t_1^{k_1}\cdots t_r^{k_r}$. The diagonal ring map $\eta:\Lambda_r\to\Lambda_1=\mathbb Z[t^{\pm1}]$, $t_i\mapsto t$, specializes the lifted chain complex by coefficient extension to the total-linking cyclic-cover chain complex. This statement does not identify $A_L\otimes_{\Lambda_r,\eta}\Lambda_1$ with the first homology of that specialized complex: homology need not commute with this nonflat base change.
thm-abelian-cover-chain-model-from-trian:
## Statement

For every finite ordered triangulation of a compact link exterior with certified positive-meridian edge loops and a label vector on each oriented edge, execution terminates. It returns exactly the finite free graded modules and boundary matrices prescribed by the procedure if and only if edge reversal, every oriented 2-simplex cocycle sum, and every marked-meridian image check pass; otherwise it returns invalid-labeling. The procedure does not recognize whether the supplied triangulation is a link exterior or whether the certified peripheral loops are genuine meridians; those are geometric input hypotheses.
thm-abelian-cover-chain-model-computes-a:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $L$ be a nonempty oriented smooth $r$-component link with $r\ge1$, compact exterior $E_L=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(L)$ obtained from pairwise-disjoint closed normal disk tubes, a finite oriented simplicial triangulation $K$ of $E_L$ with ordered vertices and simplices, with least vertex $v_0$ as the basepoint used in the cover definition, and one certified positive-meridian edge loop $\mu_i$ per component. Orient each normal disk so the positive tangent to its component followed by the positive disk basis agrees with the orientation of $S^3$, and assume the resulting classes form the standard basis of $H_1(E_L;\mathbb Z)$. If an integer-vector edge labeling is antisymmetric under edge reversal, sums to zero on every oriented 2-simplex, and evaluates to the $i$th standard basis vector on $\mu_i$, then the chain procedure returns a finite free chain complex over $\Lambda_r=\mathbb Z[t_1^{\pm1},\ldots,t_r^{\pm1}]$. The first homology of this complex is the absolute maximal-abelian-cover Alexander module $A_L$. Its Fitting ideals are independent of the triangulation and cell lifts, and its order is defined up to multiplication by a unit $\pm t_1^{k_1}\cdots t_r^{k_r}$.
